LESSON: LISTENING FOR GIST: ATTENTIVE LISTENING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ARABIC LANGUAGE
Strand: Listening and Speaking
Topic 1.5: Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening, part of Listening and Speaking in Grade 6 ARABIC LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: How can you show love to your family members? 2. How can we listen to texts attentively?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. pronounce words from minimal pairs with accuracy,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. pronounce words from minimal pairs with accuracy,

   Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. identify vocabulary on nuclear family members from an oral text for information,

   Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate attentive listening in communication for lifelong learning.

   Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. listen to an audio recording on minimal pairs and articulate the words accurately,

2. team up to record each other articulating the words,

3. organise the voice recordings recorded in a digital portfolio,

4. work jointly to identify vocabulary related to names of nuclear family members from an audio recording,

5. collaborate with peers to build a vocabulary bank on thematic words. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. listen to an audio recording on minimal pairs and articulate the words accurately,
2. team up to record each other articulating the words,
3. organise the voice recordings recorded in a digital portfolio,
4. work jointly to identify vocabulary related to names of nuclear family members from an audio recording,
5. collaborate with peers to build a vocabulary bank on thematic words. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening for Gist: Attentive Listening together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
Digital literacy: This is enhanced as the learner interacts with technology when recording each other articulating the words.

Self-efficacy: This is promoted as the learner effectively orders tasks when organising the voice recordings recorded in a digital

portfolio.

digital portfolio.

accomplish tasks.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of family members to their learning of similar concepts in Social Studies.
